facts.t: The Constitution originally said nothing about political parties
facts.d: They entered the text only with the Tenth Schedule in 1985. For thirty-five years the institutions that actually run Indian democracy had no constitutional existence at all — Article 19(1)(c) merely presupposed them.

facts.t: Six national parties were declared public authorities under RTI in 2013 — and none complied
facts.d: The Central Information Commission's ruling covered the Congress, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), BSP and NCP. More than a decade later not one has appointed a public information officer or answered an application.

facts.t: Candidates with criminal cases win three to four times more often
facts.d: ADR's analysis of the 2024 Lok Sabha found the pattern holds across parties. Criminality is not a liability at the ballot box, which is why parties keep fielding such candidates — and why reform has to target the party rather than the voter.

bank.q: Political parties first entered the constitutional text through:
bank.e: The Tenth Schedule, inserted by the 52nd Amendment in 1985. Article 19(1)(c) protects association generally but does not mention parties.

bank.q: With reference to the Election Commission's powers over parties, consider the following:
s: It may register parties under section 29A of the RoPA.
It may de-register a party for prolonged inactivity.
INC (I) v. Institute of Social Welfare limited de-registration to grounds such as fraud.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The 2002 judgment held that mere inactivity is not a ground for de-registration.

bank.q: Match List I (phase) with List II (description):
pairs: 1. Coalition era with state parties as king-makers
2. The Congress system of one-party dominance
4. Fragmentation and the first non-Congress Union government
bank.e: Congress dominance, fragmentation after 1967, the coalition era, and the present asymmetrically competitive pattern.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Central Information Commission held six national parties to be public authorities under RTI
Parties must report donations above ₹20,000 to the Election Commission
Electoral bonds were struck down in ADR v. UoI (2024)
bank.e: The exemption applies only if the party files returns, maintains audited accounts and discloses contributions.

bank.as: Germany treats political parties as constitutional actors with public responsibilities.
bank.rs: Article 21 of its Basic Law mandates internal democracy and public accounting of party funds.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the model cited for treating Indian parties as public institutions rather than private clubs.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about representation:
s: The 18th Lok Sabha has 74 women MPs, around 14%.
Women constitute roughly 46% of elected Panchayati Raj representatives.
The proportion of women MPs rose compared with 2019.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 2024 figure was slightly lower than 2019 — the gap between local and national representation is the striking contrast.

bank.q: Abhiram Singh v. C. D. Commachen (2017) held that section 123(3) bars appeals to:
o: Any candidate's or voter's religion, race, caste, community or language
Religion but not caste or language
bank.e: The broad reading — an appeal on any of those grounds by or to anyone is a corrupt practice.

bank.q: All of the following are features of Canada's party finance regime EXCEPT:
bank.e: Corporate donations are barred entirely in Canada — only individuals may give, and election expenses are partly reimbursed publicly.

bank.q: With reference to Registered Unrecognised Political Parties, consider the following:
s: Thousands never contest elections and are suspected of being money-laundering shells.
The Election Commission delisted 42 such parties in Tamil Nadu in 2025.
Maharashtra's State Election Commission now requires contesting at least five seats per five-year cycle.
bank.e: All three are correct — the minimum-contest requirement is the model reform being proposed nationally.

bank.q: Approximately what proportion of Lok Sabha members come from political families?
bank.e: About 31% in the Lok Sabha, against roughly 21% across all sitting MPs, MLAs and MLCs.

bank.q: Consider the following proposed finance reforms:
s: Real-time online disclosure of donations above ₹10,000.
A Political Finance Regulator on the model of the UK Electoral Commission.
bank.e: All three, alongside partial public funding conditional on clean-candidate norms.

bank.as: Public Interest Foundation (2018) did not create new grounds of disqualification.
bank.rs: The Court held that adding disqualification grounds is a legislative function, and directed publicity of candidates' pending cases instead.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the reason debarment at the stage of framing charges still requires legislation.
